evaluation_population.aggregate_weighting: unweighted macro-average over sampled users; no population reweighting
evaluation_population.selection_target: eligible users only; no held-out outcome stratification

item_popularity_bucket_definition.head: top 20% of catalog items by count
item_popularity_bucket_definition.long_tail: bottom 50% of catalog items by count, including zero-count items
item_popularity_bucket_definition.mid_tail: next 30% of catalog items by count

methodology_note: Because interaction timestamps are unavailable, this evaluation measures preference reconstruction/generalization under a deterministic user-stratified random holdout, not chronological next-item prediction.

metric_definitions.beyond_accuracy_scope: Coverage, novelty, popularity bias, exposure, and ILD use top-20 rankings.
metric_definitions.catalog_coverage: Unique recommended catalog IDs divided by candidate catalog size.
metric_definitions.intra_list_diversity: Mean pairwise Jaccard distance over catalog genre sets; empty/empty distance is zero.
metric_definitions.mrr: Reciprocal rank of the first test positive within the top 20.
metric_definitions.novelty_bits: Mean -log2((train positive count + 1)/(all train positives + catalog size)).
metric_definitions.popularity_bias: Mean per-user normalized-log popularity of recommendations minus training-positive history.
metric_definitions.popularity_concentration: Recommendation-event share inside train-positive popularity top 1/5/10/20%; exposure Gini includes all catalog items, including zero-exposure items.
metric_definitions.ranking: Per-user binary relevance; aggregate values are unweighted means across users.
metric_definitions.serialization: Timing covers compact ranking-ID JSON serialization, not the production HTTP response payload.

model_config.training_feedback: all observed train ratings, classes kept distinct

model_config.profile_feedback: positive training interactions folded into item space

what_this_can_tell_us: Personalized ranking quality under deterministic random held-out positive interactions.
Whether the current collaborative signal adds value over train-only popularity.
Whether LightFM collaborative challengers add value over CountSketch when included in the run.
How ranking quality changes with training-positive user activity.
Recommendation exposure and recovery across train-defined item popularity buckets.
what_this_cannot_tell_us: Chronological next-anime prediction because the source has no interaction timestamps.
Real online click-through rate or recommendation acceptance.
Production A/B-test performance without online traffic.
